newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 25.

text.p: THE DOMINION
British surgeon Keith Douglas Ramstead was found guilty of one of three counts of manslaughter in the High Court at Wellington on Thursday night, but the judge did not enter a conviction. Page 1.

Cheaper two- and three-year fixed rate mortgages are on the way for home buyers, but banks are still waiting to see whether the market settles down before lowering floating rates. The Reserve Bank on Thursday said interest rates should drop because monetary conditions were too tight. The interest rate on key

90-day bank bills dropped to 9.05 percent from 9.35 percent. Economists said on Thursday a lot depended on foreign investors' reaction overnight. If their interest remained high, rates would stabilise and banks would lower mortgage rates. Page 1.
A sixty-four-year unbroken political dynasty came to an end on Thursday as Labour's Whetu Tirakatene-Sullivan conceded defeat in the contest for the Te Tai Tonga seat. Page 1.

Labour leader Helen Clark on Thursday assured the Alliance that a Labour-led coalition government would make significant progress towards the Alliance's pollicy objectives. However, she told Alliance leader Jim Anderton that NZ First was the priority and discussions between Labour and the Alliance would have to wait. Page 2.

Briefing papers prepared by departments for the incoming government will remain secret till there are new ministers to receive them. Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen pushed on Thursday to see the papers now, saying they could be relevant to
coalition negotiations. Page 2.

The Reserve Bank unleashed the bulls on to the sharemarket on Thursday after it declared that monetary conditions had become firmer than needed. The statement caused the NZSE 40 to rocket about 44 points in just minutes after it drifted down in early trade. It closed at 2,352.91, up 32.52 on high volume of $90 million. Brokers, buoyed by the market's good performances since the election, were predicting the market would break through 2,400 sooner rather than later. Page 14.

Fletcher Challenge Canada said slow pulp and paper markets were affecting the company's financial performace, slashing first-quarter net profit to C$1.3 million (NZ$1.36 million) from $80.4 million in the September quarter of 1995. Page 14.

Hellaby Holdings aims to lift earnings to 30 cents from 25 cents a share. Managing director Tur Borren said on Thursday it would be nice to achieve the target this financial year but he gave no definite time frame. Page 14.
Weak performances by Eastern Equities' rural transport and horticulture arms have trimmed the company's full-year after-tax profit by 15 percent to $3.1 million. Page 14. THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Firefighters fear that $10 million worth of new protective gear being bought by the Fire Service may be another blunder.

Householders should be in for some mortgage relief after the Reserve Bank on Thursday gave the green light to drop interest rates. ANZ Bank chief economist Paul Stewart said the ANZ would be monitoring events and he was sure other lenders would be too. However, he cautioned that the Reserve Bank was only signalling a modest movement and would be concerned if rates fell too much.

National is understood to have given New Zealand First some early hints of just how willing it is to shift ground on crucial policies such as inflation targets and the Employment Contracts Act during Wednesday's coalition talks. The three-hour afternoon

session also apparently saw the caretaker Finance Minister Bill Birch provide New Zealand First's negotiating team with some indication of National's attitude to extra government spending. Sources, however, indicated the talks had given only very preliminary, rather than substative consideration to policy differences and specific detail and figures were not canvassed.
Former Prime Minister David Lange has ruled out becoming chairman of TVNZ, Mayor of Manukau City, or an active return to politics "in any shape or form".

A period of consolidation was the general tip for financial markets on Thursday night after comments from the Reserve Bank sent the dollar and wholesale interest rates sprawling on Thursday. But, in a potentially significant departure, further falls were predicted for the 90-day bank bill yield -- a key influence on home mortgages -- on the Futures and Options Exchange, where the December contract ended at the equivalent of 8.6 percent.
Dublin-based Independent Newspapers Plc has taken its effective stake in Wilson and Horton Ltd to 63.3 percent after picking up 18.14 percent so far in to $11 a share takeover bid.
Fletcher Challenge Canada has announced plans to split up its pulp and paper operations after a slump in September quarter profit to $C1.3 million (NZ$1.36 million).

Macraes Mining has reported that economically extractable gold reserves at the Macraes project in Central Otago had jumped 78 percent to 3.02 million ounces following the completion of a drilling programme.
The Transmark independent directors were locked in negotiations with the company's controlling shareholder Shriro Group on Thursday in an attempt to extract a better takeover offer.
